description: Leverage the 3D protein structure graph to encode a locality prior: mutations at spatially proximal positions interact more strongly than distant ones. Build a structure-aware GNN that predicts pairwise epistasis from local structural context, enabling informed pruning of the combinatorial search space to structurally coupled mutation clusters.
mathematical_formalization: Protein graph G = (V, E) where V = residues, E = contacts (C_alpha < 8A). GNN predicts epistasis: e_{ij} = GNN(h_i, h_j, d_{ij}, G). Cluster positions by thresholding |e_{ij}|. Search within clusters.
analogical_connections: Stability Oracle: graph-transformer for stability prediction
AlphaGMut: alpha shapes for mutation effect prediction
Spatial econometrics: Tobler's law — near things are more related
implementation_hypothesis: Pre-compute contact graph from PDB. Extract features via pre-trained GVP-GNN or ProteinMPNN encoder (frozen). Train MLP to predict pairwise epistasis. Training data: Mega-scale double mutants. At inference: predict epistasis, cluster, search.
experiment_seed: Train GNN on 80% Mega-scale double mutant data. Test epistasis prediction on 20% held-out proteins. Measure correlation and graph accuracy. Use predicted graph to guide search.
